deep.reconstruction:
OVERVIEW. The page holds two kinds of class-number computation for binary quadratic forms. Gauss writes a form as (a,b,c) = ax^2+2bxy+cy^2 and lists it as 'a.b', with c implied.

(A) LEFT AND MIDDLE COLUMNS: negative determinant -p, for the primes p = 1181, 1117, 1109, 1093, 1069, 1061, 1021, 1013, plus 2957 at the bottom of the middle column.
- All of these primes are 5 mod 8. Primes that are 1 mod 8 in the same range (1153, 1129, 1097, 1049, 1033) are deliberately skipped.
- Each heading reads 'p.h', where h is the class number of forms of determinant -p.
- Under it, row k gives the reduced (or nearly reduced) representative a.b of g^k. Here g is the class of a small form: (3,1,(p+1)/3) when 3 is represented; otherwise (11,4) for 1117, (19,3) for 1093, (10,1) for 1069, (7,1) for 1021.
- Every entry satisfies a | p+b^2, so c = (p+b^2)/a. For example, 1181: (3,1,394), (9,4,133), (27,13,50); then 81 reduces to (17,14,81); then (31,20,51), (14,11,93), (35,17,42), (37,22,45), (15,8,83), (5,3,238), (15,13,90).
- Since p = 5 mod 8, the 2-part of the class group is Z/2. Its nontrivial element is the ambiguous form (2,1,(p+1)/2), and h/2 is odd.
- Each table therefore runs k = 0..h/2 and ends with g^{h/2} = (2,1), entered simply as '2'. Rows: 1117 has 0..7 with h=14; 1093 has 0..5 with h=10; 1061 has 0..13 with h=26; 1021 has 0..11 with h=22; 1109 has 0..25 with h=50.
- The last rows are back-filled from the end, using g^{h/2-j} = (2,1)·g^{-j}. Their leading coefficients are therefore 2a(g^j) after reduction, e.g. ...18, 6, 2 for 1109 and 1061.
- For 1181, rows 12-14 read 30, 10, 30. These are (2,1)·g^{-11}, (2,1)·g^{-10}, (2,1)·g^{-9} [my reconstruction], i.e. 2·15, 2·5, 2·15.
- Direct composition [mine]: (15,13)(3,1) gives (45,13,30), equivalent to (30,-13,45) = (2,1)·(15,13)^{-1}. Hence g^23 = (2,1) and ord g = 46.
- So the heading number is found, or at least confirmed, by meeting the ambiguous form. This is the procedure of Disquisitiones Arithmeticae, arts. 305-307.
- Sample of the composition check [mine]: for 1117, (13,12)(11,4) gives (143,103,82), which reduces to (19,2,59), matching row 5. Also (2,1)(37,-20) gives (74,17,19), which reduces to (19,2) as well.
- The 2957.54 table lists powers of (3,1) for k = 0..17: (9,7), (27,16), (38,11), (47,45), (21,2), (7,2), (21,16), (51,35), (17,1), (51,1), (37,22), (31,9), (49,9), (43,28), (29,1), (34,1). Rows 18-27 are unfinished.

(B) TOTALS IN THE MIDDLE COLUMN.
- '8. 50.46.30.26.26.22 14.10 / 224. 28' means: 8 primes on this page; class numbers sorted; sum 224; mean 28.
- '36. 1064' adds this to the running total carried from the previous page ('28.840.30'): 28+8 = 36 primes and 840+224 = 1064.
- 'Chil.' is a per-chiliad summary for primes p = 5 mod 8. Chiliad 1: 43 primes, sum of h = 630. Chiliad 2: 36 primes, sum 1064. Chiliad 3: 30(?) primes, sum 1256 (both numbers overwritten).
- The third numbers 38, 70, 82 are probably the maximal h in each chiliad. The starred column 0, 0, 1 counts some exceptional case (meaning uncertain; perhaps non-cyclic groups, or a non-generating base form).
- This is Gauss's empirical study of the mean growth of class numbers (cf. DA art. 302).

(C) RIGHT COLUMN, 'Divis. formae □ - a': positive determinant p, for p = 2969, 2957, 2953, 2917, 2909, 2897, 2861, 2857. All are primes = 1 mod 4.
- Listed are the numbers Q_n of the continued-fraction algorithm for sqrt(p): P_0=0, Q_0=1, a_n = floor((sqrt p + P_n)/Q_n), P_{n+1} = a_n Q_n - P_n, Q_{n+1} = (p - P_{n+1}^2)/Q_n.
- These are the |a| of the reduced forms in the principal cycle, i.e. 'divisors' of x^2 - p. Example, 2957: Q = 1, 41, 53, 44, 59, 23, 11, 68, 37, 4, 89, 17, 44, 29, 29.
- Gauss stops at the repeated value ('29.29 &c'). That is the symmetric centre of an odd period, so x^2 - p y^2 = -1 is solvable.
- When the class number exceeds 1, all cycles are listed with labels k.(h-k), pairing a class with its inverse.
- For 2917 = 54^2 + 1 (h = 9): the principal cycle is (1), and the others are (3,71,36), (9,89,12), (4,27,79) and (12,59,47,36,43), all of which I verified.
- For 2857 (h = 3): '0.3' marks the principal cycle 1, 48, 21, 56, 47, 39, 19, 24, 27, 63, 32, 51, 51; '1.2' marks a non-principal cycle beginning with 3.
errors: 2953, principal cycle: the computed sequence is ...27, 31, 24, 23, 48, 3, 83, 24, 53, 53. The transcribed '29' between 24 and 48 should be 23 (Gauss's slip or a misreading). The overwritten '[5/6]3' must be 53.
2957 (positive determinant): Q_1 = 2957 - 54^2 = 41. The overwrite at '1.4?' resolves to 41; reading it as 44 would be wrong.
1021 table, row 3: (31,8,35) is correct, since 1021+64 = 31·35. The overwritten digit must be 31; '33.8' is impossible because 33 does not divide 1085.
Several entries are written with an unreduced middle coefficient, e.g. 26.21 for 1093, 47.45 and 51.35 for 2957, 25.23 for 1021. The first coefficients are still correct, so this is harmless.

For 1181, rows 15-23 are left blank and rows 12-14 omit b. For 1069 (rows 9-15), 1013 (rows 8-13) and 2957.54 (rows 18-27) the tables are unfinished. In these cases h is asserted rather than fully exhibited on the page (perhaps known from elsewhere).

results.what: Class numbers h(-p) for primes p = 5 mod 8. Method: the cyclic chain of powers of a small form, reduced at each step, until the ambiguous form (2,1,(p+1)/2) is reached; this gives h = 2k. Values: 1181:46, 1117:14, 1109:50, 1093:10, 1069:30, 1061:26, 1021:22, 1013:26, 2957:54.
results.modern_name: Class group computation for imaginary quadratic orders via composition and reduction (order of an element, cyclic class group)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss, Disquisitiones Arithmeticae (1801), arts. 305-307; class-number tables in Werke II

results.what: Chiliad statistics: number of primes p = 5 mod 8, sum and mean of h(-p) (and probably the maximum) per thousand: 43/630, 36/1064, 30?/1256
results.modern_name: Empirical average order of class numbers (Gauss's mean-value conjecture, later proved by Lipschitz/Mertens)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (DA art. 302; Nachlass tables published by Schering/Dedekind in Werke II)

results.what: Cycles of reduced forms (continued-fraction remainders Q_n of sqrt p) for prime positive determinants p = 1 mod 4 near 2900. Symmetric centre detected, so the period is odd and the negative Pell equation is solvable. All cycles listed when h>1 (2917: h = 9; 2857: h = 3).
results.modern_name: Continued fraction of sqrt(p) / infrastructure of reduced forms; class numbers of real quadratic orders
results.usually_credited_to: Lagrange (continued fractions), Gauss (cycles, DA arts. 183-187); tables in Gauss Werke II

deep.surprise_reason: These are working sheets for Gauss's known class-number tables for negative and positive prime determinants. They use his published DA methods, and the chiliad sums tie into his known study of average class numbers. Nothing beyond what is attributed to him already.

checkable.asserts: Every entry a.b of the 1181 table defines an integral form of determinant -1181.
(15,13)(3,1) composes to (45,13,30), equivalent to (30,-13,45) = (2,1)(15,13)^-1. Hence g^23 is the ambiguous class and g has order 46.
Row 3 of the 1021 table is 31.8, not 33.8.
The 2957.54 power chain consists of valid forms of determinant -2957.

checkable.sympy: (lambda p: sum(1 for a in range(1,int((p/3)**0.5)+2) for b in range(-(a//2),a//2+1) if (p+b*b)%a==0 and (p+b*b)//a>=a and not (b<0 and (2*abs(b)==a or (p+b*b)//a==a))))(1181) == 46
checkable.asserts: Gauss's class number h = 46 for determinant -1181, counting reduced forms ax^2+2bxy+cy^2 with ac-b^2 = p.
The remaining class numbers in the headings.
The page and chiliad running totals.
The principal cycle Q_n of sqrt(2957) is 1, 41, 53, 44, ..., 29, 29.
The non-principal cycles of determinant 2917 are (3,71,36), (9,89,12), (4,27,79) and (12,59,47,36,43).
